descricao: Curated list used by sbr_lookup.py. 'fora' = subjects outside the scope/the collection (the lookup only says 'the Reference does not cover it' for them or for terms with no occurrence in sbr_terms.json). 'so_ponteiro' = subjects that the Reference mentions but the package does not summarize (the lookup returns the page pointer and the note).

fora.nota: GraalVM/native image/AOT: 0 occurrences in the Reference 2.7.18 (neither a chapter nor a mention).
Boot 3.x is not covered: the text is the 2.7.18 line (Java 8-21, javax.*).
the jakarta.* namespace is not used in the text; it only appears in artifact coordinates in Appendix F.
the text declares Java 8 as the minimum and compatibility up to Java 21 (SBR p.27); Java 17 as a baseline is a Boot 3 thing.
Resilience4j/Hystrix do not exist in the Reference; 'circuit breaker' is only mentioned in passing (see its own entry).
Observation API, Micrometer Tracing and OpenTelemetry: 0 occurrences; only Micrometer metrics and a mention of Sleuth/Zipkin.
Docker Compose and @ServiceConnection do not exist in the Reference 2.7.18 (Testcontainers only with @DynamicPropertySource, SBR p.647-650).
SSL bundles: 0 occurrences (only server.ssl.* and client-specific SSL exist).
KRaft: 0 occurrences; ZooKeeper appears in non-Kafka contexts (config data p.96; Appendix F p.686, 875).
Quarkus, MapStruct and the JavaCodeGeeks practical guide (Spring Boot 3) belong to java-backend-frameworks-expert; they are not part of this collection.
Grafana: 0 occurrences; the Reference only carries the Prometheus scrape_config (SBR p.494).

the build-image goal/task (buildpacks) does not appear in the Reference: the text only says that the Maven and Gradle plugins support buildpacks and refers to the plugin documentation (SBR p.439, 550).
fora.encaminhar: plugin documentation / java-backend-frameworks-expert (the Boot 3 guide carries bootBuildImage)

fora.nota: Spring Test's @Rollback, @Commit and @Sql: 0 occurrences; for tests without rollback the Reference shows @Transactional(propagation = Propagation.NOT_SUPPORTED) (SBR p.190-191).

the Reference does NOT cover Spring Cloud Config; the only occurrence in the text (SBR p.857, Appendix F.1) is the name of the artifact log4j-spring-cloud-config-client, a managed version, not a description of the product. For remote configuration the book only carries the pluggable spring.config.import mechanism (SBR p.96).

so_ponteiro.nota: mentioned in passing on p.464 (readiness probes: shared external systems, 'the application could have circuit breakers and fallbacks'); the Reference carries neither Resilience4j nor circuit breaker configuration.
mentioned only in passing (Prometheus exemplars p.494; HTTP tracing p.518); no configuration.
ZooKeeper appears as an example of an external config data source (p.96) and in Appendix F coordinates; not as part of Kafka configuration.
p.388: once retries are exhausted, the message is rejected and discarded or routed to a dead-letter exchange 'if the broker is configured'; the Reference does not carry how to declare a DLX/DLQ.
spring.kafka.consumer.auto-offset-reset exists in Appendix A (short description, no default); the Reference does not explain offset semantics.
the package records only the pointer (@AutoConfigureRestDocs with MockMvc, WebTestClient and REST Assured, p.203-214).
Spock 2.x cited in one paragraph (spock-spring); no details.
Apache Geode only cited (Spring Boot for Apache Geode is a separate project).

management.metrics.export.statsd.step.d: window used to compute windowed statistics such as max; the Reference says to align the step with the collector's scrape interval to benefit from them (default 1m)

management.metrics.export.statsd.polling.d: gauge polling frequency; on reading, the value is recomputed and sent if it changed (or always, if publish-unchanged-meters=true) (default 10s)

management.metrics.export.statsd.buffere.d: accumulates measurements before sending them to the StatsD server (default true)

management.metrics.export.statsd.max-pac.d: total size of a payload, which must fit in the network MTU (default 1400)

management.metrics.export.stackdriver.ba.d: number of measurements per request; if there are more, several requests are made (default 10000)

management.metrics.export.stackdriver.st.d: reporting frequency (default 1m); the body shows 30s as an example

management.metrics.export.stackdriver.pr.d: identifier of the monitored Google Cloud project

management.metrics.export.stackdriver.us.d: false publishes counters as GAUGE; true as CUMULATIVE (default false)

management.metrics.export.stackdriver.re.d: type of the monitored resource (default global)

management.metrics.export.wavefront.batc.d: number of measurements per request; if there are more, several requests (default 10000)

management.metrics.export.wavefront.repo.d: report histogram distributions aggregated per minute (default true)

management.metrics.export.datadog.applic.d: application key; not mandatory, but improves the experience (sends descriptions, types and base units)

management.metrics.export.datadog.uri.d: where to send; change it to publish to a Datadog site outside the US or to an internal proxy (default https://api.datadoghq.com)

management.metrics.export.prometheus.des.d: publish descriptions in the scrape payload; turn off to reduce the volume per scrape (default true)

management.metrics.export.prometheus.his.d: histogram type for DistributionSummary and Timer (default prometheus)

management.metrics.export.defaults.enabl.d: turns all default exporters on/off (default true)

management.metrics.use-global-registry.d: bind the auto-configured MeterRegistry instances to the global static Metrics registry; in tests use false to isolate (default true)

management.metrics.web.server.request.me.d: name of the meter for received requests (default http.server.requests)

management.metrics.web.client.request.me.d: name of the meter for sent requests (default http.client.requests)

management.metrics.web.server.max-uri-ta.d: maximum number of distinct values of the uri tag; above it new metrics are denied by a filter (default 100)

management.metrics.system.diskspace.path.d: paths for which to report disk metrics (default .)

management.metrics.tags.*.d: common tags applied to every meter

management.metrics.enable.*.d: turns meters on/off by name prefix; the longest match wins; the key all applies to everything

management.metrics.distribution.percenti.d: publish percentile histograms (aggregable) for meters with the name prefix; only takes effect on systems that support them

management.metrics.distribution.slo.*.d: SLO limits by name prefix; one counter per limit is published

management.endpoint.health.show-details.d: when to show health details: never, when-authorized or always (default never)

management.endpoint.health.show-componen.d: when to show the components; if absent show-details applies

management.endpoint.health.roles.d: roles that authorize seeing details; empty = every authenticated user is authorized

management.endpoint.health.status.order.d: severity order of the statuses (default DOWN, OUT_OF_SERVICE, UP, UNKNOWN)

management.endpoint.health.status.http-m.d: map of health status to HTTP code; by default DOWN and OUT_OF_SERVICE give 503

management.endpoint.health.logging.slow-.d: time from which a slow indicator generates a log warning (default 10s)

management.endpoint.health.probes.enable.d: turns the liveness/readiness groups on in any environment (default false; turned on by themselves only on Kubernetes)

management.endpoint.health.probes.add-ad.d: publishes liveness and readiness on the main port at /livez and /readyz (default false)

management.endpoint.health.group.*.d: health groups (include, exclude, show-details, roles, status, additional-path)

management.health.diskspace.threshold.d: minimum free space required by the diskspace indicator (default 10MB)

management.health.db.ignore-routing-data.d: ignore AbstractRoutingDataSource when building the database indicators (default false)

management.endpoint.logfile.external-fil.d: external log file to serve, useful when the log goes out through redirection and not through the logging system

management.endpoint.env.keys-to-sanitize.d: masked keys (replaces the defaults); accepts simple suffixes or regex

management.endpoint.env.additional-keys-.d: masked keys in addition to the defaults (sum)

management.endpoint.configprops.keys-to-.d: masked keys in configprops (replaces the defaults)

management.endpoint.configprops.addition.d: masked keys in configprops in addition to the defaults (sum)

management.endpoints.web.cors.allowed-or.d: allowed origins; without origins or origin-patterns CORS is off; with credentials * cannot be used

management.endpoints.web.cors.allowed-me.d: allowed methods; when absent only GET applies

management.endpoints.web.cors.max-age.d: cache time of the pre-flight response (default 1800s)

management.endpoints.web.base-path.d: prefix of the web endpoints (default /actuator); relative to the context-path (or the WebFlux base-path), or to management.server.base-path when there is its own port

management.endpoints.web.path-mapping.*.d: maps the ID of an endpoint to another path

management.endpoints.web.exposure.includ.d: IDs of endpoints exposed on the web, or * for all (default only health)

management.endpoints.web.exposure.exclud.d: IDs excluded from exposure; exclude beats include

management.endpoints.jmx.domain.d: JMX domain of the endpoints (default org.springframework.boot; falls back to spring.jmx.default-domain if set)

management.info.git.mode.d: how to expose git.properties: simple (default) or full

management.server.port.d: HTTP port of the management endpoints (default the same as the application); -1 turns HTTP off

management.server.address.d: bind address of management; requires its own port

management.trace.http.include.d: items included in the HTTP trace (default request-headers without Authorization and Cookie, response-headers without Set-Cookie, and time)

server.port.d: HTTP port of the server (default 8080); 0 = random; -1 turns HTTP off keeping the context

server.shutdown.d: supported shutdown type: immediate (default) or graceful

server.http2.enabled.d: turns HTTP/2 on if the environment supports it (default false); h2 with SSL, h2c without SSL

server.forward-headers-strategy.d: how to handle the X-Forwarded-* headers: NATIVE, FRAMEWORK or NONE (default NATIVE on Cloud Foundry, Heroku and Kubernetes; NONE otherwise)

server.tomcat.redirect-context-root.d: redirect requests to the context root by appending / (default true); with SSL terminated at the proxy set false

server.tomcat.remoteip.internal-proxies.d: regex of trusted proxies; the default covers private ranges and loopback (10.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x, 127.x, 100.64-127, 172.16-31 and ::1); empty trusts everyone (not in production)

server.tomcat.remoteip.remote-ip-header.d: header from which to extract the remote IP (e.g. X-Forwarded-For); setting this or protocol-header turns the RemoteIpValve on

server.tomcat.remoteip.protocol-header.d: header with the incoming protocol (usually X-Forwarded-Proto); setting this or remote-ip-header turns the RemoteIpValve on

server.tomcat.threads.max.d: maximum number of Tomcat worker threads (default 200)

server.tomcat.accept-count.d: maximum size of the connection queue when all threads are busy (default 100)

server.tomcat.max-connections.d: maximum number of connections accepted and processed at the same time (default 8192)

server.tomcat.basedir.d: Tomcat base directory; without a value it uses a temporary directory (relevant for the access logs)

server.tomcat.mbeanregistry.enabled.d: turns the Tomcat MBean Registry on (default false); required for the tomcat.* meters

server.tomcat.accesslog.enabled.d: turns the Tomcat access log on (default false)

server.undertow.accesslog.enabled.d: turns the Undertow access log on (default false)

server.jetty.accesslog.enabled.d: turns the Jetty access log on (default false); without filename it goes to System.err

server.servlet.session.timeout.d: session timeout (default 30m); without a duration suffix, seconds

server.servlet.register-default-servlet.d: register the default Servlet in the container (default false)

server.servlet.encoding.mapping.*.d: map of locale to response charset

server.error.include-stacktrace.d: when to include the trace attribute in the error response (default never)

server.error.whitelabel.enabled.d: default error page for browsers (default true)

spring.data.cassandra.contact-points.d: addresses of the cluster nodes in host:port format, or just host to use the configured port (default [127.0.0.1:9042])

spring.data.cassandra.local-datacenter.d: name of the driver's local datacenter; the book usually gives keyspace-name, contact-points and the local datacenter together

spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto.d: Hibernate DDL behavior; default create-drop with an embedded database without a schema manager, none in the other cases

spring.sql.init.mode.d: when to run schema.sql/data.sql: embedded (default), always or never

spring.jpa.defer-datasource-initializati.d: defers initialization by SQL scripts until after Hibernate creates the schema (default false)

spring.ldap.embedded.base-dn.d: base DN(s) of the embedded LDAP server (UnboundID); several entries require a list (YAML) or an index [0],[1] (properties)

spring.security.filter.dispatcher-types.d: dispatcher types of the security filter (default async, error, request)

spring.devtools.restart.poll-interval.d: interval between checks for classpath changes (default 1s)

spring.devtools.restart.quiet-period.d: time without changes required before restarting (default 400ms)

management.metrics.export.atlas.lwc-step.d: step (frequency) of streaming to Atlas LWC, the highest resolution of the on-demand stream; Reference rule: it must be less than or equal to atlas.step AND atlas.step must be an even (integer) multiple of lwc-step; e.g. step 1m with lwc-step 7s violates it (60/7 is not an integer) (default 5s)

management.metrics.export.atlas.lwc-enab.d: turns streaming to Atlas LWC on (default false)

management.metrics.export.atlas.lwc-igno.d: ignores in streaming the expressions with the same step as the normal publication to Atlas, for when the data already goes to Atlas (default true)

management.metrics.export.atlas.meter-ti.d: lifetime of a meter with no activity: after the period it expires and is no longer reported (default 15m)

management.metrics.export.atlas.batch-si.d: measurements per request; if there are more, several requests (default 10000); for Atlas it is on p.780 and for Datadog on p.782

management.metrics.export.atlas.config-t.d: lifetime of the subscriptions coming from the LWC service (default 150s)

management.metrics.export.atlas.config-r.d: frequency of refreshing the configuration from the LWC service (default 10s)

management.metrics.export.atlas.step.d: Atlas step (reporting frequency); must be an even multiple of lwc-step (default 1m)

management.metrics.export.datadog.batch-.d: measurements per request; if there are more, several requests (default 10000)

server.undertow.max-headers.d: maximum number of headers accepted, a limit against hash collision attacks; NO published default: the default cell is empty in Appendix A (confirmed on p.766)

server.undertow.max-parameters.d: maximum number of query/path parameters, a limit against hash collisions; NO published default (empty cell, p.766)

server.undertow.threads.io.d: worker I/O threads; NO value in the default column: the description only says it is derived from the number of available processors (p.766)

server.undertow.no-request-timeout.d: idle time of a connection without processing a request before it is closed; NO published default (empty cell, p.766)

server.undertow.threads.worker.d: worker threads; the default is IN THE DESCRIPTION, not in the column: 8 times the number of I/O threads (p.766)

spring.servlet.multipart.file-size-thres.d: threshold from which received files are written to disk (default 0B: everything goes to disk; derived reading)

spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size.d: maximum size of each file (default 1MB; -1 = unlimited)

spring.activemq.pool.block-if-full.d: when the pool is full and someone asks for a connection: blocks (true) or throws "JMSException" (false)

spring.activemq.pool.block-if-full-timeo.d: maximum blocking time before throwing an exception if the pool is still full (the book's description does not explicitly condition it on block-if-full; the natural reading is that it matters when you choose to block) (default -1ms)

spring.activemq.pool.enabled.d: turns on the use of a JmsPoolConnectionFactory in place of the plain ConnectionFactory (default false)

spring.activemq.pool.idle-timeout.d: idle time of a pool connection (default 30s)

spring.activemq.pool.max-connections.d: maximum number of connections in the pool (default 1)

spring.activemq.pool.max-sessions-per-co.d: maximum number of sessions per connection in the pool (default 500)

spring.activemq.pool.time-between-expira.d: interval between runs of the thread that removes idle connections; a negative value = no removal thread runs (default -1ms)

spring.activemq.pool.use-anonymous-produ.d: uses a single shared anonymous MessageProducer (default true)

spring.artemis.pool.block-if-full.d: when the pool is full and someone asks for a connection: blocks (true) or throws "JMSException" (false)

spring.artemis.pool.block-if-full-timeou.d: maximum blocking time before throwing an exception if the pool is still full (the book's description does not explicitly condition it on block-if-full; the natural reading is that it matters when you choose to block) (default -1ms)

spring.artemis.pool.enabled.d: turns on the use of a JmsPoolConnectionFactory in place of the plain ConnectionFactory (default false)

spring.artemis.pool.idle-timeout.d: idle time of a pool connection (default 30s)

spring.artemis.pool.max-connections.d: maximum number of connections in the pool (default 1)

spring.artemis.pool.max-sessions-per-con.d: maximum number of sessions per connection in the pool (default 500)

spring.artemis.pool.time-between-expirat.d: interval between runs of the thread that removes idle connections; a negative value = no removal thread runs (default -1ms)

spring.artemis.pool.use-anonymous-produc.d: uses a single shared anonymous MessageProducer (default true)

spring.rabbitmq.port.d: RabbitMQ port; ignored if addresses is set; the default is IN THE DESCRIPTION (empty column): 5672, or 5671 with SSL on (p.735)

spring.jta.atomikos.properties.log-base-.d: directory where the Atomikos transaction log files are kept; the default is IN THE DESCRIPTION (empty column): the current working directory (p.707)

spring.task.scheduling.thread-name-prefi.d: prefix of the task scheduler thread names; the default is "scheduling-"

spring.cache.redis.time-to-live.d: expiration of cache entries; by default entries NEVER expire (the 'default' is written in the description; the default column is empty)

management.metrics.export.influx.retenti.d: period for which Influx retains data in the current database; the '7d' that appears in the description is only an EXAMPLE of a duration format, not a default; InfluxDB v1 only
retention policy to use; if not given, Influx writes to the DEFAULT retention policy (server behavior described, not a property value); InfluxDB v1 only

management.metrics.export.appoptics.api-.d: AppOptics API token, used to authenticate the sending of metrics; Appendix A does not publish a default value (empty cell), so it must be provided when the backend is on [inference about being mandatory; the book only describes it as the token]

management.metrics.export.appoptics.batc.d: how many measurements per request; if there are more, several requests are made (default 500)

management.metrics.export.appoptics.conn.d: maximum time to connect to the backend in requests (default 5s)

management.metrics.export.appoptics.enab.d: turns metrics export to this backend on/off (default true)

management.metrics.export.appoptics.floo.d: sends the time rounded down (aligns measurements from several hosts to the same time boundary) (default false)

management.metrics.export.appoptics.host.d: tag that is mapped to the "@host" attribute when sending metrics to AppOptics (default instance)

management.metrics.export.appoptics.read.d: maximum time to read the backend response (default 10s)

management.metrics.export.appoptics.uri.d: URL of the AppOptics endpoint to which the metrics are sent (default https://api.appoptics.com/v1/measurements)

spring.quartz.auto-startup.d: starts the scheduler automatically after initialization (default true)

spring.quartz.jdbc.comment-prefix.d: single-line comment prefixes in the initialization SQL scripts (default [#, --])

spring.quartz.jdbc.initialize-schema.d: Quartz schema initialization mode: embedded (default) or always (book example); the book warns that the default Quartz scripts DROP tables and triggers on every restart (p.416)

spring.quartz.jdbc.platform.d: platform used in the @@platform@@ placeholder of the initialization scripts; detected automatically by default (no published value)

spring.quartz.jdbc.schema.d: path of the SQL script that initializes the schema (default: the Quartz tables_@@platform@@.sql scripts on the classpath)

spring.quartz.job-store-type.d: Quartz job store type: memory (default) or jdbc (requires a DataSource)

spring.quartz.overwrite-existing-jobs.d: whether jobs defined by configuration overwrite those already saved in the persistent store (default false)

spring.quartz.properties.*.d: map of additional properties passed to the Quartz scheduler; this is where advanced Quartz configuration goes (p.416); the native Quartz names (thread pool, misfire etc.) are NOT in the book: citing them is [extrapolation]; spring.quartz.thread-pool-size and spring.quartz.misfire-threshold do NOT exist in Appendix A

spring.quartz.startup-delay.d: delay to start the scheduler after initialization finishes; useful if no job should run before the application is fully up (default 0s)

spring.quartz.wait-for-jobs-to-complete-.d: wait for running jobs to finish on shutdown (default false)

spring.devtools.remote.secret.d: shared secret required to establish the remote connection; enables remote support (and the server endpoint) when set; no published default; the client reads it from the properties on the same classpath

spring.devtools.remote.secret-header-nam.d: HTTP header in which the secret travels (default X-AUTH-TOKEN)

spring.devtools.remote.proxy.host.d: proxy host used by the remote client to reach the remote application; no published default

spring.devtools.remote.proxy.port.d: proxy port used by the remote client; no published default

spring.devtools.remote.context-path.d: context path that serves the remote connection (default /.~~spring-boot!~)

debug.d: debug mode: with --debug (or debug=true) some core loggers (embedded container, Hibernate, Spring Boot) emit more information; it does not put the whole application in DEBUG (default false)

trace.d: trace mode: with --trace (or trace=true) turns on trace logging of some core loggers (embedded container, Hibernate schema generation, the whole Spring portfolio) (default false; line at the end of table A.1, p.676)

spring.kafka.streams.application-id.d: application.id of Kafka Streams; the Default column is empty, but the Appendix A description refers to spring.application.name as the default (the body repeats this)

spring.webflux.multipart.file-storage-di.d: directory where parts larger than max-in-memory-size are kept; default: folder "spring-multipart" under the system temporary directory; ignored with streaming=true

spring.webflux.multipart.max-in-memory-s.d: maximum memory per part before writing to disk (default 256KB; -1 = everything in memory); ignored with streaming=true

spring.webflux.multipart.max-disk-usage-.d: maximum disk space per part (default -1B = no limit); ignored with streaming=true

spring.webflux.multipart.max-parts.d: maximum number of parts per multipart request (default -1 = no limit)

spring.webflux.multipart.max-headers-siz.d: maximum memory per header section of each part (default 10KB; -1 = no limit)

spring.webflux.multipart.headers-charset.d: charset used to decode headers (default UTF-8)

spring.webflux.multipart.streaming.d: if true, reads straight from the input buffer, without keeping it in memory or in a file (default false = not streaming)

spring.datasource.name.d: datasource name, used ONLY if generate-unique-name=false; default "testdb" with an embedded database, otherwise null

spring.datasource.jndi-name.d: JNDI location of the datasource; when set, class, url, username and password are ignored

spring.datasource.generate-unique-name.d: generates a random name for the datasource (default true); with true, spring.datasource.name is not used

management.metrics.export.ganglia.time-t.d: Ganglia multicast TTL: must be one above the number of hops (routers) between the hosts, i.e. hops+1 (default 1)

management.metrics.export.ganglia.addres.d: UDP addressing mode, unicast or multicast (default multicast)

management.metrics.export.graphite.graph.d: uses Graphite tags instead of hierarchical naming; no default in the column: on by default unless tags-as-prefix is set

management.metrics.export.graphite.tags-.d: in hierarchical naming, turns the listed tag keys into part of the metric prefix; ignored if graphite-tags-enabled is true (default empty list)

spring.redis.jedis.pool.enabled.d: turns the connection pool on; enables itself if commons-pool2 is on the classpath; in Jedis the pool is implicitly on in sentinel mode and this key only applies to a single node

spring.redis.jedis.pool.max-active.d: maximum connections allocated at the same time by the pool; negative value = no limit (default 8)

spring.redis.jedis.pool.max-idle.d: maximum idle connections in the pool; negative value = unlimited (default 8)

spring.redis.jedis.pool.max-wait.d: maximum time that allocating a connection blocks before throwing an exception when the pool is exhausted; negative value = blocks indefinitely (default -1ms)

spring.redis.jedis.pool.min-idle.d: minimum target of idle connections kept in the pool; only takes effect if it and time-between-eviction-runs are positive (default 0)

spring.redis.jedis.pool.time-between-evi.d: interval between runs of the thread that evicts idle connections; positive turns the thread on, otherwise there is no eviction (no published default)

spring.redis.lettuce.pool.enabled.d: turns the connection pool on; enables itself if commons-pool2 is on the classpath

spring.redis.lettuce.pool.max-active.d: maximum connections allocated at the same time by the pool; negative value = no limit (default 8)

spring.redis.lettuce.pool.max-idle.d: maximum idle connections in the pool; negative value = unlimited (default 8)

spring.redis.lettuce.pool.max-wait.d: maximum time that allocating a connection blocks before throwing an exception when the pool is exhausted; negative value = blocks indefinitely (default -1ms)

spring.redis.lettuce.pool.min-idle.d: minimum target of idle connections kept in the pool; only takes effect if it and time-between-eviction-runs are positive (default 0)

spring.redis.lettuce.pool.time-between-e.d: interval between runs of the thread that evicts idle connections; positive turns the thread on, otherwise there is no eviction (no published default)

spring.messages.use-code-as-default-mess.d: uses the message code itself as the default message instead of throwing NoSuchMessageException when the code is not resolved; recommended only in development (default false)

spring.redis.lettuce.cluster.refresh.ada.d: uses adaptive refresh of the cluster topology with all available refresh triggers (default false)

spring.redis.lettuce.cluster.refresh.dyn.d: discovers and queries all cluster nodes to obtain the topology; with false only the initial seed nodes are the source (default true)

spring.activemq.send-timeout.d: time to wait for a response when sending messages; 0 means wait forever (default 0ms)

spring.activemq.non-blocking-redelivery.d: if true, stops delivery before redelivering messages of a rolled-back transaction; implies that message order is NOT preserved (default false)

spring.rabbitmq.channel-rpc-timeout.d: continuation timeout of RPC calls on channels; zero means wait forever (default 10m)

spring.rabbitmq.connection-timeout.d: connection timeout; zero means wait forever (the default column is empty)

spring.rabbitmq.requested-channel-max.d: number of channels per connection requested by the client; 0 means unlimited (default 2047)

spring.jdbc.template.fetch-size.d: rows fetched from the database each time needed; -1 uses the JDBC driver's default setting (default -1)

spring.jdbc.template.max-rows.d: maximum rows; -1 uses the JDBC driver's default setting (default -1)

server.tomcat.keep-alive-timeout.d: wait for another HTTP request before closing the connection; without a value it uses the connectionTimeout; -1 means no timeout

server.tomcat.processor-cache.d: maximum idle processors kept in cache; -1 leaves the cache unlimited (theoretical ceiling = maximum threads, according to the Appendix A description)

server.undertow.max-http-post-size.d: maximum size of the HTTP POST content; -1 (the default) means unlimited

descricoes_nota: Short paraphrases (from the package, not from the book) of the meaning of Appendix A properties; 'ap' = Appendix A page(s) where the key, description and default are; 'corpo' = page(s) of the Reference body that describe the subject. Properties without an entry here: the package keeps only key+default; read the description on the Appendix A page.

contexto_pagina.nota: p.544-545 is Spring Boot CLI context, NOT overriding a version in Maven/Gradle. To override a managed version: SBR p.42 (NOTE) and Appendix F.2, table of *.version properties, SBR p.876-881 (e.g. hibernate.version p.878); for the CLI: references/12.
